args.title: deviation-analysis-memo.docx
args.body:
DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet — Counterparty Markup Review
Practice Area: Banking & Finance
Output: deviation-analysis-memo.docx

TO: Deal Partner / Client Working Group
FROM: Banking & Finance Counsel
RE: Counterparty Markup Deviation Analysis — Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet
DATE: [Engagement Date]

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

We compared the counterparty’s (borrower-side) markup of the Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet against the firm’s base term sheet and deal materials, cross-referencing (i) the disclosure schedules and exhibits, (ii) the controlling partner instructions in the deal-team correspondence, and (iii) the financial / liability profile implied by the scheduled retained liabilities and pending regulatory matters.

The markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  (1) Indemnification: silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar) basket;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect (MAE): new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue in this matter; and
  (3) Survival / limitation period: a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, in direct conflict with Exhibit B’s survival matrix.

Controlling partner instruction (latest message in the deal-team thread; earlier contrary priority ordering is superseded): the client will concede the basket conversion, but any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue.

Recommendation snapshot (detail in §§ III–V):

  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): CONCEDE per partner instruction.
  • Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT / restore firm-standard cap; Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities make a silent cap cut economically material.
  • MAE regulatory carve-outs: REJECT / narrow; Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries make the carve-out case-specific and unacceptable.
  • Survival-period reduction: REJECT — WALK-AWAY. Restore Exhibit B survival matrix for core representations.

================================================================================
II. SCOPE, SOURCES, AND METHODOLOGY
================================================================================

A. Base Materials
  • Original / firm-standard Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet and operative deal materials (Matter File 3 — Banking Finance), including representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination architecture.
  • Practice posture: firm-standard banking-finance precedent and market practice for senior secured credit facilities.

B. Counterparty Markup
  • Borrower-side revision identifying three principal deviation clusters (indemnification cap and basket; MAE definition; survival / limitation period).

C. Schedules and Exhibits (controlling over general base-material statements)
  • Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the markup’s MAE regulatory carve-outs.
  • Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup’s indemnification changes would silently shift.
  • Exhibit B — survival matrix contradicted by the markup’s limitation-period change.
  • Principle: scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base banking-finance materials.

D. Partner Instructions (Deal-Team Correspondence)
  • Latest message controls: client will concede the basket conversion; survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue.
  • Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and must not drive the analysis.

E. Financial / Economic Overlay
  • No separate numeric term-sheet grid was supplied beyond the liability and regulatory profile in the schedules. Economic analysis therefore keys off (i) Schedule 5.2 retained-liability shift risk under a reduced cap and tipping basket and (ii) Schedule 3.7 regulatory-inquiry exposure under a weakened MAE. Both amplify the dollar and risk significance of Deviations 1 and 2 relative to a clean credit.

F. Method
  For each deviation we (1) state the base position, (2) state the markup change, (3) reconcile schedules/exhibits, (4) apply partner instructions and financial overlay, and (5) assign Accept / Reject / Counter with negotiation posture.

================================================================================
III. DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP AND BASKET
================================================================================

A. Base Position (Firm-Standard Term Sheet)
  • Indemnification cap at firm-standard level for a senior secured credit facility of this profile.
  • Basket structured as a deductible: indemnifiable losses recoverable only above the basket threshold; amounts within the basket remain with the indemnified party (lender) until the threshold is cleared, and recovery is of excess only (true deductible), not first-dollar after tipping.

B. Markup Change
  1. Silent reduction of the indemnification cap (amount lowered without conspicuous redline call-out or negotiation footnote).
  2. Conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket (once the threshold is reached, recovery is from dollar one).

C. Schedule / Exhibit Reconciliation
  • Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. Under the markup, those retained liabilities would be silently shifted in economic incidence: a lower cap truncates upside recovery on large retained items, while a tipping basket accelerates first-dollar exposure once the (often modest) threshold is crossed.
  • Because scheduled exceptions control over general base statements, Schedule 5.2 is the operative financial data for sizing this deviation. The combination of known retained liabilities + silent cap cut is not a drafting nicety; it is a balance-sheet transfer away from the lender group.

D. Partner Instruction
  • Basket conversion: CONCEDE. Client will accept deductible → tipping.
  • Cap reduction: not authorized for concession. Partner instruction is silent on conceding the cap; default is hold firm-standard cap, especially given Schedule 5.2.

E. Financial Overlay
  • Retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 make any unnegotiated cap reduction a direct reduction in expected recovery. Silent presentation increases execution risk (missed in business review).
  • Tipping vs. deductible: economic cost of tipping is real but secondary and, per partner, acceptable as a negotiated give.

F. Disposition
  • Basket (deductible → tipping): ACCEPT / CONCEDE per controlling partner instruction. Document the concession expressly in the issues list so it is not reopened.
  • Cap reduction: REJECT. Counter: restore firm-standard indemnification cap; require any cap movement to be bilateral, priced, and footnoted against Schedule 5.2 retained-liability exposure. Flag the “silent” character of the cut as process failure — future markups must call out quantum changes.

G. Proposed Counter-Language (conceptual)
  • Reinsert base cap quantum and formula.
  • Basket: “tipping basket” formulation acceptable; threshold quantum to remain as in base or as separately agreed.
  • Add: “For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section reduces the Cap below [Base Cap], and Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain fully subject to the Cap and survival terms in Exhibit B.”

================================================================================
IV. DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT DEFINITION (REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS)
================================================================================

A. Base Position
  • MAE definition in the firm-standard senior secured term sheet does not carve out regulatory action of the type implicated by this credit (standard MAE construct with limited, market-standard carve-outs that do not neutralize known regulatory risk).

B. Markup Change
  • MAE definition is amended to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter — i.e., the carve-out is tailored to neutralize the precise regulatory risk profile of this borrower / facility.

C. Schedule / Exhibit Reconciliation
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup’s MAE regulatory carve-outs.
  • Effect: if the carve-outs stand, events arising from or related to the Schedule 3.7 inquiries (and like regulatory action) would be excluded from MAE, gutting MAE-based draw-stop, default, pricing, and related lender protections precisely where the credit is most exposed.
  • Scheduled exceptions control: Schedule 3.7 is not background color; it is the reason this carve-out is unacceptable on this deal.

D. Partner Instruction
  • No concession authorized on MAE regulatory carve-outs. Partner priority ranking focuses the walk-away on survival, but does not authorize acceptance of MAE weakening tied to known inquiries.

E. Financial Overlay
  • Pending inquiries create identifiable downside paths (fines, operational constraints, license / authorization risk) that can impair repayment capacity and collateral value. Stripping those paths from MAE reallocates that downside entirely to lenders without price adjustment in the markup.

F. Disposition
  • REJECT the regulatory-action carve-outs as drafted.
  • Counter options (in descending preference):
    (1) Delete the new regulatory carve-outs entirely and restore base MAE;
    (2) If commercial pressure requires limited carve-out language, confine it to generally applicable changes in law of prospective effect only, expressly excluding (i) the Schedule 3.7 matters, (ii) any expansion, adverse development, or resolution of those matters, and (iii) enforcement, consent orders, or penalties directed at the Borrower or its Subsidiaries; and require a separate MAE / condition construct tied to Schedule 3.7;
    (3) Price any residual carve-out with a margin step-up, additional reporting, and enhanced default / cash dominion triggers tied to regulatory milestones.
  • Diligence / documentation follow-ups: refresh status of both Schedule 3.7 inquiries before commitment finalization; align MAE, conditions precedent, and ongoing information covenants to the same regulatory inventory.

G. Proposed Counter-Language (conceptual)
  • MAE carve-out rider: “excluding any Regulatory Action, inquiry, proceeding, or development relating to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7 or any matter of the same character affecting the Borrower or its Subsidiaries.”
  • Or full deletion of the markup’s regulatory carve-out clause.

================================================================================
V. DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
================================================================================

A. Base Position
  • Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for representations and warranties, including extended or core survival for fundamental / core representations customary on a senior secured facility (and any specially negotiated items).

B. Markup Change
  • A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

C. Schedule / Exhibit Reconciliation
  • Exhibit B is the controlling survival schedule. The markup’s limitation-period change is a direct conflict with Exhibit B, not a clarification.
  • Interaction with Deviation 1: shortened survival on core reps plus a reduced indemnification cap compounds lender loss — claims may both time-bar earlier and hit a lower ceiling.
  • Interaction with Schedule 5.2: retained liabilities that surface after the shortened period become unrecoverable even if within the (already reduced) cap.

D. Partner Instruction — CONTROLLING
  • Any survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue.
  • Earlier deal-team messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded. This memorandum follows only the latest instruction.

E. Financial Overlay
  • Shortened core-rep survival reduces the expected value of indemnity coverage on the highest-severity breach categories (organization, authority, enforceability, solvency, priority of liens, etc.), which is inconsistent with senior secured economics and with the retained-liability profile on Schedule 5.2.

F. Disposition
  • REJECT — WALK-AWAY. Do not proceed to definitive documentation with shortened core-rep survival.
  • Required position: restore Exhibit B survival matrix in full for core representations; any non-core survival trim, if discussed at all, must be itemized, scheduled, and approved separately — and even then is not authorized by current partner instruction.
  • Negotiation posture: communicate walk-away clearly; do not trade survival against the already-conceded basket conversion. Basket concession is the give; survival is not available as a further give.

G. Proposed Counter-Language (conceptual)
  • “The representations and warranties shall survive as set forth on Exhibit B, which controls over any general limitation period in this Agreement. Without limiting Exhibit B, core representations shall survive for [Exhibit B period] (or indefinitely, if so provided on Exhibit B).”
  • Delete markup limitation-period language insofar as it purports to override Exhibit B.

================================================================================
VI. CROSS-DEVIATION AND HOLISTIC RISK
================================================================================

The three deviations are not independent:

  1. Cap ↓ + tipping basket + Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities → higher frequency / lower ceiling recovery dynamic; basket tip is conceded, cap cut is not.
  2. MAE regulatory carve-outs + Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries → MAE remedy hollowed out on the live risk.
  3. Survival ↓ vs. Exhibit B + (1) and (2) → time-barred or definitionally excluded claims on the same risk clusters.

Net effect if markup accepted as-is: lenders retain senior secured labels while losing (i) quantum, (ii) MAE trigger integrity on known regulatory exposure, and (iii) time-on-risk for core reps — an unacceptable package under firm playbook norms for senior secured credit and under the controlling partner instruction.

Playbook / market-practice alignment (banking-finance senior secured):
  • Hold firm-standard indemnity caps unless priced and disclosed.
  • MAE carve-outs must not erase scheduled, deal-specific regulatory matters.
  • Survival matrices in exhibits control; silent or general limitation periods that cut core-rep survival are off-market for lender-side senior secured paper and, here, are expressly walk-away.

================================================================================
VII. RECONCILIATION CHECKLIST (EVERY DEVIATION ADDRESSED)
================================================================================

Markup item                              | Base / Control source        | Schedule / Exhibit touchpoint      | Partner instruction        | Disposition
-----------------------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------|----------------------------|---------------------------
Indemnification cap silently reduced     | Firm-standard cap            | Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities  | No concession              | REJECT / restore cap
Basket: deductible → tipping             | Deductible basket            | Schedule 5.2 (incidence shift)     | CONCEDE (latest message)   | ACCEPT / CONCEDE
MAE: regulatory-action carve-outs        | Base MAE (no such carve-out) | Schedule 3.7 two pending inquiries | No concession              | REJECT / narrow or delete
Limitation period shortens core-rep      | Exhibit B survival matrix    | Exhibit B direct conflict;         | WALK-AWAY                  | REJECT — WALK-AWAY
  survival                                 |                              | compounds cap / Schedule 5.2       | (latest message controls)  | restore Exhibit B

Distractor materials (unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled in the matter folder) were identified and are not relied upon.

================================================================================
VIII. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS
================================================================================

1. Issue this memorandum to the deal partner and confirm walk-away authority on survival remains current.
2. Transmit a markup response / issues list reflecting:
     • Concede tipping basket (document as client give);
     • Restore indemnification cap; require conspicuous negotiation of any quantum change keyed to Schedule 5.2;
     • Delete or tightly ring-fence MAE regulatory carve-outs relative to Schedule 3.7;
     • Restore Exhibit B survival matrix; state survival reduction is non-negotiable / walk-away.
3. Refresh diligence on Schedule 3.7 inquiries and quantify Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities for any residual commercial discussion on cap.
4. Do not circulate a commitment or long-form credit agreement incorporating the survival cut or the unring-fenced MAE regulatory carve-outs.
5. Calendar a counsel alignment call focused solely on Deviation 3 (survival) if counterparty resists, with express walk-away preparation.

================================================================================
IX. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

Of the three counterparty deviations, only the indemnification basket conversion (deductible → tipping) is within the client’s authorized concession under the controlling partner instruction. The silent indemnification cap reduction must be rejected and the firm-standard cap restored in light of Schedule 5.2. The MAE regulatory carve-outs must be rejected or narrowly redrawn so they cannot neutralize the Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries. The shortened survival / limitation period for core representations conflicts with Exhibit B and is a walk-away issue; Exhibit B must control.

This memorandum reconciles the counterparty markup against the base banking-finance materials, the schedules and exhibits (which control over general base statements), the financial liability / regulatory profile reflected in those schedules, and the latest partner instructions. Every identified deviation is addressed above.

— End of Memorandum —
